news.headline: SECP issues final notices in Unity Foods unusual-trading probe; probe tied to separate FIA criminal case over alleged multi-billion-rupee irregularities
news.summary: SECP issued final notices on Sept 2, 2026 to four individuals - CEO Muhammad Farrukh, Safdar Sajjad, Fehmida Amin and Hina Safdar - requiring them to appear before its Karachi investigation team on Sept 3, 2026, after they neither appeared nor requested rescheduling from an Aug 31 summons, per ProPakistani. The formal SECP investigation (opened June 2, 2026 under Section 139 of the Securities Act 2015) covers alleged unusual/insider trading in Unity Foods Limited (PSX: UNITY) shares; Farrukh is specifically required to explain and provide records on the pledging of UNITY shares with banks. Per search-indexed reporting (ProPakistani, Business Recorder, TechJuice headlines), this SECP probe separately led to an FIA criminal case (around Aug 31, 2026) against Unity Foods' former management over alleged multi-billion-rupee financial irregularities; one search result cited a discrepancy of about Rs44.7bn between published accounts and internal records, not independently confirmed via a directly-fetched primary article this cycle. No PSX trading halt/suspension of UNITY shares reported in sources checked. Logged as impact 5 (severe - fraud/criminal-case allegations, default per desk criteria Rule 10); escalation flagged.

news.headline: Pakistani rupee records gain against US dollar
news.summary: The Pakistani rupee closed at Rs277.45/USD on Wednesday Sept 2, 2026, gaining Re0.01 versus Tuesday Sept 1's close of Rs277.46/USD, per Business Recorder's 'Intra-day update: rupee records gain against US dollar'. The dollar stayed broadly firm as renewed Middle East hostilities pushed oil prices higher and revived inflation concerns. Negligible single-day FX move; logged as impact 1 (routine), consistent with prior similarly small FX moves in this newslog.

news.headline: PSX: Stocks end marginally higher amid volatile trading
news.summary: KSE-100 confirmed close Thu Sept 3, 2026 at 174,929.68, up 153.09 points (+0.09%) from Wed Sept 2's confirmed close of 174,776.60 (already logged); intraday high 175,796.24, low 174,893.67, per Business Recorder ('PSX: Stocks end marginally higher amid volatile trading'). Index opened with strong buying, climbed sharply, then gave back most gains on late profit-taking before closing marginally higher. Positive momentum driven by automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser and oil & gas exploration companies; index heavyweights HUBCO (HUBC), MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MCB, MEBL and UBL traded positive. Business Recorder cited Pakistan's $3bn Eurobond sale (separately logged this cycle) and continued Strait of Hormuz-related oil volatility as sentiment drivers. Sub-1% net move; impact 3 (notable), consistent with prior similar-magnitude index-close entries in this newslog.

news.source: Business Recorder / ProPakistani / Dawn.com / Aaj English
news.headline: Pakistan raises record $3bn through largest-ever dual-tranche Eurobond sale
news.summary: Pakistan raised $3 billion through a dual-tranche Eurobond sale announced Sept 3, 2026 - $1.75bn via a 5.5-year bond at a 7.5% coupon and $1.25bn via a 10-year bond at 7.9% - drawing nearly $6bn in orders (almost double the amount issued) from a broad, diversified base of institutional investors, per Business Recorder, ProPakistani, Dawn.com and Aaj English TV. Described as Pakistan's largest-ever single international bond issuance; proceeds earmarked for external financing needs including debt repayments. This confirms/upgrades the already-logged Aug 25, 2026 item ('Pakistan eyes $1-2bn return to global capital markets', impact 3) from a pending plan to a completed, priced transaction of larger size. Logged as impact 4 (material - confirmed major sovereign financing deal / sharp positive macro-financing development, per desk criteria Rule 10); escalation flagged.

news.headline: PSX: Volatility at bourse, KSE-100 gains nearly 400 points
news.summary: KSE-100 confirmed close Fri Sept 4, 2026 at 175,328.82, up 399.14 points (+0.23%) from Thu Sept 3's confirmed close of 174,929.68 (already logged); intraday high 175,418.29, low 174,515.38, after opening weak and recovering on midday/late buying. No company-specific driver named; article cites global sentiment lift after a Fed official cooled rate-hike fears. Sub-1% net move; impact 3 (notable), consistent with prior similar-magnitude index-close entries in this newslog.

news.headline: PSX partners with UK's MOBILIST programme for climate/sustainable investment
news.summary: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX: PSX) announced a partnership with the UK government's MOBILIST programme to mobilise private investment in Pakistan's sustainable development and climate transition via listed products, supporting future IPOs and new SDG/net-zero-aligned listed instruments (cites the Parwaaz Green Action Bond as a prior example); no financial figures or transaction disclosed. Officials: Alison Blackburne (UK Deputy High Commissioner Karachi), Farrukh H. Sabzwari (PSX MD/CEO). Logged as impact 3 (notable strategic/institutional initiative, per desk criteria Rule 10), no immediate earnings impact.

news.headline: PSX: Volatility keeps KSE-100 Index flat
news.summary: KSE-100 confirmed close Fri Sept 4, 2026 at 175,328.82, up 399.14 points (+0.23%) from Thu Sept 3's confirmed close of 174,929.68 (already logged); intraday low 174,515.38, high 175,418.29, per Business Recorder ('PSX: Volatility keeps KSE-100 Index flat'). Index opened weak, fell sharply from ~175,300 to the intraday low, then recovered on buying interest that emerged around midday and accelerated into the close; article attributes broader positive tone partly to a Federal Reserve official cooling US rate-hike fears and a global Asian-shares rally, no Pakistan-specific stock/sector driver named. Sub-1% net move; impact 3 (notable), consistent with prior similar-magnitude index-close entries in this newslog.

news.headline: Pakistan Cables approves CECL's buy-back on entire stake for Rs350mn
news.summary: Pakistan Cables Limited (PSX: PCAL) approved the sale of its entire 17% shareholding (4,845,000 ordinary shares) in Chinoy Engineering & Construction (CECL) back to CECL at approximately Rs72.24/share, totaling approximately Rs350 million, per a company notice to PSX dated Sept 4, 2026 reported by Business Recorder. Transaction subject to corporate, regulatory and shareholder approvals; upon completion PCAL will hold zero shares in CECL. Logged as impact 2 (minor company item - divestment of a non-core minority stake, not a major contract or earnings event), per desk criteria Rule 10.

news.headline: Diesel price rises Rs3.74, petrol falls Rs3.13 per litre
news.summary: OGRA/federal government adjustment effective Saturday Sept 5 through Monday Sept 7, 2026: petrol cut Rs3.13/litre to Rs345.87/litre; HSD diesel raised Rs3.74/litre to Rs378.05/litre, per Business Recorder, citing international oil market conditions. Routine fortnightly-mechanism adjustment, consistent with prior similarly small moves logged.

news.headline: PSX: KSE-100 sheds nearly 1% amid selling pressure
news.summary: KSE-100 confirmed close Mon Sept 7, 2026 at 173,636.07, down 1,692.75 points (-0.97%) from Friday Sept 4's confirmed close of 175,328.82 (already logged), per Business Recorder (3:55pm update, 'PSX: KSE-100 sheds nearly 1% amid selling pressure'). Third consecutive session of losses tied to the ongoing US-Iran conflict (following the Aug 31 impact-5 shock and Sept 2 impact-4 session, both already logged); index-heavy stocks named trading red across Business Recorder's rolling coverage of the session include OGDC (-2.38%), Pakistan Refinery/PRL (-10%), NBP (-1.27%), PPL (-1.88%), SSGC (-2.37%), plus ARL/ATRL, HUBCO, PSO, FFC, MEBL and UBL named earlier in the day. Sectors hit: automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, OMCs, refineries. Cited drivers: renewed US-Iran military tensions pushing oil prices higher, plus global inflation/rate-hike concerns. Logged as impact 4 (material, sharp market-wide move tied to continuing geopolitical/war shock, per desk criteria Rule 10), consistent with the Sept 2 entry of similar magnitude and cause.

news.headline: Rupee registers gain against US dollar
news.summary: The Pakistani rupee closed at Rs277.40/USD on Monday Sept 7, 2026, a gain of Re0.01 versus the prior close, as the dollar weakened internationally amid Middle East tensions and rising oil prices, per Business Recorder. Open-market dollar rates Rs277.95 (buying) / Rs278.45 (selling). Negligible single-day FX move; logged as impact 1 (routine), consistent with prior similarly small FX moves in this newslog.

news.headline: PSX: KSE-100 sheds nearly 1,000 points amid geopolitical uncertainty
news.summary: KSE-100 confirmed close Tue Sept 8, 2026 at 172,642.16, down 993.91 points (-0.57%) from Mon Sept 7's confirmed close of 173,636.08 (already logged); intraday high 173,736.19, low 171,490.00, per Business Recorder ('PSX: KSE-100 sheds nearly 1,000 points amid geopolitical uncertainty'). Fourth consecutive losing session tied to the ongoing US-Iran conflict (following Aug 31 impact-5 shock, Sept 2 and Sept 7 impact-4 sessions, all already logged); index initially traded near 173,500 before selling intensified around noon on fears of a prolonged Middle East conflict after Iran threatened retaliation against further US strikes, with oil prices rising on supply concerns. Sectors hit: automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, OMCs. Index-heavy stocks named trading red: PSO, MARI, POL, MEBL, NBP, UBL. Secondary indices: BR100 19,014 (-131.1/-0.68%), KSE30 51,415 (-288.5/-0.56%), BR30 69,547 (-386.1/-0.55%). Sub-1% net move, smaller magnitude than the prior two impact-4 sessions; logged as impact 3 (notable), per desk criteria Rule 10.

news.headline: OGDC posts record Rs242.4bn profit, declares highest-ever annual dividend
news.summary: Oil & Gas Development Company Limited (PSX: OGDC) reported net profit after tax of Rs242.374 billion for FY26 (year ended June 30, 2026), up 43% YoY, with EPS of Rs56.35 versus Rs39.50 prior year, per The Nation (published Sept 5, 2026, following a board meeting held Sept 4, 2026). The board declared a final cash dividend of Rs6.00/share (60%), taking total FY26 dividend to Rs17.00/share (170%) including Rs11.00/share already paid as interim dividends - described as the company's highest-ever annual dividend. Net sales revenue was Rs449.191 billion; OGDC contributed Rs187 billion to the national exchequer via taxes, dividends and royalties. Logged as impact 4 (material earnings surprise plus record dividend, per desk criteria Rule 10) for this core-tier constituent; escalation flagged.

news.headline: PSX: KSE-100 sheds nearly 1,000 points amid geopolitical uncertainty (afternoon rolling update)
news.summary: Confirms the already-logged Sept 8, 2026 confirmed close of 172,642.16 (-993.92pts/-0.57%) versus Mon Sept 7's close of 173,636.08; Business Recorder's rolling coverage additionally noted the index fell as much as ~2,145 points intraday before recovering into the close, with selling in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks and OMCs on prolonged US-Iran conflict fears after Iran threatened retaliation against further US strikes. Tagged to the union of tickers from the already-logged confirmed-close item; no new company-specific driver added.

news.headline: SE Fruits & Vegetables secures PSX approval for IPO to raise up to Rs1.92bn
news.summary: Sargodha-based fruit/vegetable exporter SE Fruits & Vegetables Limited (formerly Shaheen Enterprises) received PSX approval on Sept 7, 2026 to offer 30 million ordinary shares (32.01% of post-IPO capital) via book-building, floor price Rs40/share, max price Rs64/share, to raise Rs1.2bn-Rs1.92bn; lead managers Topline Securities and Growth Securities. Not yet a listed constituent of the desk universe. Logged as impact 2 (minor company item - pre-listing IPO approval), per desk criteria Rule 10.
